reasoning_content: The CMS is currently being built (with the app also running, so about 2.5GB in use). I'll wait for the CMS to respond.

action.command:
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  if curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 http://127.0.0.1:41487/ 2>/dev/null; then echo "cms responding"; break; fi
  sleep 55
done
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "cms direct: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:41487/ 2>/dev/null || echo "cms not yet"
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "app still: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:43189/ 2>/dev/null || echo "app down"
free -m | sed -n '2p'

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments:
{"command": "for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  if curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 http://127.0.0.1:41487/ 2>/dev/null; then echo "cms responding"; break; fi
  sleep 55
done
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "cms direct: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:41487/ 2>/dev/null || echo "cms not yet"
curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 3 -w "app still: %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:43189/ 2>/dev/null || echo "app down"
free -m | sed -n '2p'", "security_risk": "LOW", "summary": "Wait for cms dev server to respond"}

summary: Wait for cms dev server to respond
